analysis: Macro still owns the tape, but Nvidia's buyback is the first real counterweight since 6 AM. The $150B add (total $235B, the largest US buyback ever) is a cash-generation statement timed against investor unease over Nvidia's $99B in AI equity investments; the +2% pop is modest given the size, showing the oil/yield/Fed-hike repricing is crowding out company news. Two new AI-sentiment negatives: MongoDB's CEO defecting to Meta effective immediately (-17%) and OpenAI halting training for safeguards (single outlet, unconfirmed) — alongside Meta posting back-to-back losses for the first time since mid-August. Versus the 6 AM brief: buyback, MDB-CEO, Boeing glitch, Kodiak +89%, and the open prints are all new; the Iran-rejection/oil/yield story is unchanged, with front-month Brent near $108 keeping the pressure on. Signal: oil-yields-October-hike chain into PCE/jobs week, plus whether AI sentiment keeps slipping. Noise: thin premarket flashes in GOOGL/AMZN and the Aave tokenized-stock story.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Nvidia board approved a $150B increase to its share-repurchase program, bringing total authorization to $235B — the largest-ever US buyback, topping Apple's $110B (May 2024). NVDA rose ~1.8-2% early Monday, reversing earlier losses. Execution expected through fiscal 2028 (ends Jan 2028).
headlines.why_it_matters: Massive capital-return signal of cash confidence; could soothe concerns over Nvidia's $99B of AI equity investments, though the pop is modest against the macro drag.

headlines.headline: Stocks opened lower Monday: Dow fell nearly 400 points (-0.8%), S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.5%. Pre-open futures had recovered somewhat (Dow futures -0.5%, S&P -0.3%, Nasdaq-100 -0.5%).
headlines.why_it_matters: No relief at the open; the market is still pricing the weekend's oil/yield shock, with tech leading the decline on duration sensitivity.

headlines.headline: Crude and yields still elevated into the open: WTI +1.9% to $94.13 after hitting $96.54 earlier; Brent's December contract +3.6% to $100.98 with the November front-month near $108; 10Y Treasury at 5.24%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Oil spike keeps inflation and October-hike repricing alive; the Brent front-month/Dec spread shows acute near-term supply anxiety.

headlines.headline: MongoDB president and CEO Chirantan Desai resigned effective immediately to 'pursue a senior role' at Meta, per the company. MDB tumbled 17%; Meta fell 1.5%, on pace for back-to-back losses for the first time since mid-August.
headlines.why_it_matters: Sudden CEO exit is a leadership shock for MongoDB; for Meta, a senior AI-talent hire arriving as its stock shows rare back-to-back weakness.

headlines.headline: OpenAI halted training of its latest models to implement additional safeguards, per Barron's, adding to pressure on AI-related stocks including Meta.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile; if true, a safety-pause headline that feeds AI-capex and model-risk anxiety.

headlines.headline: Boeing fell 2.6% after the WSJ reported the company identified a software glitch that could disrupt an automated landing feature; Boeing told Barron's its engineers are working on a permanent update.
headlines.why_it_matters: Report-driven selloff, not an official company disclosure; the fix-in-progress response limits, but doesn't erase, the overhang.

headlines.headline: Energy stocks bid on crude: Chevron +1.4%, ExxonMobil +1.5%, with APA, Baker Hughes, Devon Energy, Diamondback, and Halliburton also up. AI chip names weak premarket: Intel -2.3%, Sandisk -2.8%, with AMD, Corning, Dell, Marvell, Micron lower.
headlines.why_it_matters: Classic macro rotation into the open: energy winners, rate-sensitive tech losers.

headlines.headline: Kodiak Sciences surged 89% after two experimental eye drugs met their primary goal in a late-stage study, positioning the biopharma for its first product.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source (company announcement via Barron's); binary clinical-trial upside, idiosyncratic and unrelated to the macro tape.
